source.probe: hb-shape widths of a 64k-character Arabic report per class; box = Word hhea 1810/1050 over 2048

note:
Sakkal Majalla (M365 cloud face Word renders real) is a compact naskh
with a narrow Latin. Class scales are shaped widths of a 64k-char Arabic
report in the cloud cuts vs the stand-in (harfbuzz over the real files,
2026-09-30): Arabic letters 0.8055 of the Noto Naskh subset (bold cut
0.841; registered weight-normal so Blink synthesizes bold), Arabic-Indic
digits 0.9396, and vs Liberation Sans/Helvetica: ASCII digits 0.7287,
space 0.545, punctuation 0.6667, letters 0.67, dashes 0.9113, other Latin-1
and general punctuation symbols 0.66 (they would otherwise fall to Al Bayan,
whose 1.5 em box stretches the line). Weight-normal only: Blink
serves one weight group per family, so a bold group without the Arabic
ranges would send bold Arabic past the alias to Geeza Pro; bold runs are
synthesized and keep the regular ratios (bold cuts run 4-12% wider).
Letters sit in a second family so a run's own ascii face still wins them
(chain splice in line-metrics.ts). Every face pins the Word hhea box
1810/1050 over 2048.
